1. Clicking the purple ring at [18, 57] → orange square moved from [12, 24] to [16, 38]

3. Clicking the orange square at [15, 31] → moved to [15, 29]
4. Clicking the orange square at [15, 29] → no movement
5. Clicking the orange ring at [51, 40] → no movement
6. Clicking the purple square at [41, 49] → no movement
7. Clicking the orange square at [15, 29] again → no movement
8. Clicking the white marker at [15, 32] → no movement
The only thing that caused movement was clicking the purple ring. Maybe I need to click the purple ring again to activate the orange square.
But wait, let me reconsider the game. In Level 1:
- Clicking the ring moved the square toward the ring
- Clicking the square also moved it toward the ring
- The square consumed the gray diamond on the path
- When the square reached the ring, the level was complete
In Level 2, maybe the mechanic is different. Let me look at the initial state more carefully. From the very first frame of Level 2:
- White diamond at [6, 17] (this is the marker)
- Orange square at [12, 24]
- Purple square at [41, 49]
- Gray diamonds at [9, 49], [21, 8], [35, 45], [48, 54]
- Purple ring at [18, 57]
- Orange ring at [51, 40]

- Orange square moved from [12, 24] to [16, 38]
- White diamond moved from [6, 17] to [18, 57]
- The gray diamond at [9, 49] was consumed (it had an orange center)
So the purple ring activation caused:
1. Orange square to move along its path
2. White diamond to move to the purple ring's position
3. Gray diamond at [9, 49] to be consumed
The white diamond at [18, 57] was the marker for the purple ring. But now the white marker is at [15, 32], which is near the orange square.
Wait, maybe the white marker moved from [18, 57] to [15, 32] as the orange square moved. The white marker tracks the orange square's position on the path.
Actually, looking at the white marker pixels:
- [13, 31], [14, 32], [15, 33], [16, 32], [17, 31]
This forms a diamond shape centered at [15, 32]. The orange square is at [15, 29], which is 3 columns to the left.
Maybe the white marker indicates where the orange square SHOULD be, not where it currently is. The orange square needs to move to [15, 32] to align with the marker.
But clicking the orange square didn't move it. Maybe I need to click the purple ring again to "push" the orange square forward.
